newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's key industrial index accelerates fall.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's key industrial index accelerates fall.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index clocked its seventh consecutive loss and largest yet on Wednesday, depressed by continued selling in a market short of buyers, brokers said.

The industrial index dropped 122.63 or 1.1 percent to close at 10,598.16, some 381.94 points or 3.5 percent off its all time record 10 980.10 set on April 24, reinforcing fears firming money market rates are looking more attractive.
"There is a lot of nervousness from an institutional point of view as to where rates are going and that is impacting on the share market," one broker told Reuters.

Short term interest rates have risen more than five percent since last week to around 21 percent but the broker said further movement beyond 23 percent was unlikely given the level of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's rediscount rate at 23.5 percent.
Analysts say the share market, which has been distracted by a number of new issues, should find strength from from expected strong corporate results, including market leaders Delta corporation.

Counters to lose on Wednesday included retailers Truworths which dropped 60 cents to 950 and Tedco which was off 20 cents to 240 cents. Millers National Foods also dropped 20 cents to 500 while Delta at 1,770 eased by 30 and bankers NMB lost 50 cents to 3,250.
The mining index also dropped 1.1 percent or 11.11 points, weighed down by lower deals in coal miners Wankie, down 25 cents at 525, and gold miners Falgold, which lost four cents at 65.
The mining index closed at 1,006.17, some 559 points or 35.7 percent off its previous all time of 1,565 reached one year ago last week.
